title: CBIC mandates immediate halt on GST arrests
where: Economy, page 23 (Aanchal Magazine); letter on Reforms 3.0, page 13
syllabus: GS3 › Government budgeting; Tax reform · GS2 › Government policies; Transparency and accountability · GS4 › Trust in governance
summary: CBIC has told its field offices to stop GST arrests and to apply the GST Council's relaxed rules on e-way bill checks and show-cause notices before the law is amended.
ideas: From suspicion to trust: the GST Council recommended removing the power of arrest by omitting Section 69 of the CGST Act; CBIC has stopped arrests now, ahead of the amendments due from April 1, 2027.
GS3 · Tax reform
Removing arrest powers moves GST towards trust-based tax administration.

Inspection only on intelligence: vehicles can be stopped only on specific intelligence authorised in writing by an officer not below Joint Commissioner, and only by the supplier's or recipient's state.
GS2 · Accountability
Written reasons and senior authorisation curb harassment through random roadside checks.
Small cases out of litigation: a minimum ₹10,000 threshold for show-cause notices aims to cut low-value disputes and compliance costs.
GS3 · Ease of doing business
Thresholds for notices reduce low-value litigation and compliance costs.
Law must follow intent: experts warned the Council's recommendations lack legal force until Parliament and states amend their GST laws, so the interim order fills the gap.
GS2 · Rule of law / Cooperative federalism
Council recommendations need legislative backing in Parliament and states to bind officers.
Part of a wider trust agenda: readers urge self-declaration, deemed approvals and statutory timelines for routine permissions, with time-bound grievance redress.
GS2 · Governance reform
Trust-based governance treats citizens as honest stakeholders through self-declaration and deemed approvals.
keywords: Assuming honesty and targeting enforcement at risk
Trust-based compliance focuses enforcement on high-risk cases, not every taxpayer.
Using intelligence and data to choose whom to inspect
Risk-based enforcement replaces random checks with intelligence-led action.
Permission treated as granted if not decided in time
Deemed approvals shift the cost of delay from citizens to the state.
Discretionary inspection powers that invite harassment
Curbing roadside GST checks reduces inspector raj.
The GST Council is India's leading example of cooperative federalism.
data: Minimum threshold for issuing GST show-cause notices
A ₹10,000 floor on show-cause notices will cut low-value GST disputes.
Centre's fiscal deficit in April-September as a share of the full-year target (36.5% a year ago)
The Centre used 42.1% of its full-year fiscal deficit target in the first half (CGA).
examples: Removal of the power to arrest under GST
Dropping GST arrest powers is an example of decriminalising economic offences.
CBIC applying reforms before the law is amended
GS2 · Executive action / GS4 · Spirit of the law
CBIC's interim order shows administrators acting on the spirit of a reform before the letter arrives.
pyqs: Transparency and accountability as building stakeholders' trust through the rule of law.
Taxes subsumed in GST and its revenue implications.
potential: "Trust-based governance is the next frontier of tax reform in India." Discuss with reference to GST. (10 marks)

title: Nine months and five bribes for a death certificate
news: An octogenarian in Gurugram needed nine months and repeated bribe demands, from ₹4,000 to ₹25,000, to get her sister's death certificate, whose official fee was ₹30.
syllabus: Probity in governance: citizen's charters, quality of service delivery, challenges of corruption
link: Petty corruption at the counter turns a citizen's right into a favour and hits the old and the grieving hardest; trust-based reforms mean little if service delivery stays extractive.
question: "Petty corruption in routine services erodes trust in the State more than grand scams do." Discuss with examples.

title: When corruption costs power
news: A student-led movement in Serbia, sparked by a deadly canopy collapse seen as a symbol of alleged corruption, won elections and unseated the President after over a decade.
syllabus: Corruption and probity in governance · Accountability
link: Corruption erodes public trust until citizens demand accountability; a peaceful, organised movement turned that anger into political change.
question: "Unchecked corruption ultimately erodes the legitimacy of those in power." Discuss with examples.

title: RBI to hire agency to manage social media presence
syllabus: GS2 › E-governance; Transparency and accountability · GS3 › Monetary policy and its communication · GS4 › Citizen-centric governance; Quality of service delivery
summary: The RBI has invited bids for an agency to run its social media round the clock, with podcasts, digital content and responses to the public, to communicate better in a digital-first information environment.
ideas: E-governance: the RBI is taking its policies, decisions and public-awareness messages directly to citizens through social media and podcasts.
GS2 · E-governance
The RBI's round-the-clock social media outreach shows public institutions adapting to a digital-first information environment.
Clear communication strengthens monetary policy: when people understand the central bank's signals, policy works better.
GS3 · Monetary policy
Effective communication by the RBI makes monetary policy more credible and effective.
People-centric good governance: listening to online conversations and answering the public makes an institution more transparent and responsive.
GS4 · Citizen-centric governance
By tracking and answering public responses online, the RBI models citizen-centric, responsive governance.
keywords: A setting where people get information mainly online
Public institutions must communicate effectively in a digital-first information environment.
Governance designed around citizens' needs and feedback
Two-way digital outreach makes governance citizen-centric.
How the RBI explains its policy to markets and the public
Clear central bank communication anchors public expectations.
examples: 24x7 social media, podcasts, digital content and public responses, run by its Department of Communication
The RBI's 2026 move to run 24x7 social media and podcasts is a best practice in people-centric governance.
pyqs: Good governance and e-governance: the RBI's direct digital outreach to citizens is an example.

title: Privacy versus the public's right to know
news: News publishers have challenged the data protection law for requiring a person's consent before journalists process their data.
syllabus: Information sharing and transparency in government · Ethical issues in media
link: Respect for individual privacy must be weighed against the public's right to know about matters of public interest.
question: As an editor, you hold verified evidence of a senior official's misuse of public funds, but he invokes his privacy and refuses consent. What will you do and why?
